### Types of data

```{=html}
<figure class="petra-diagram diagram-tree" aria-label="Types of data: categorical and numerical; numerical data may be discrete or continuous">
<div class="diagram-root">Types of data</div>
<div class="diagram-branches">
<section class="diagram-branch">
<div class="diagram-node">Categorical</div>
<p>Categorical data represents groups or categories.</p>
<p><strong>Examples:</strong></p>
<ol><li>Car brands: Audi, BMW and Mercedes.</li><li>Answers to yes/no questions: yes and no</li></ol>
</section>
<section class="diagram-branch">
<div class="diagram-node">Numerical</div>
<div class="diagram-leaves"><div>Discrete</div><div>Continuous</div></div>
<p>Numerical data represents numbers. It is divided into two groups: discrete and continuous. Discrete data can be usually counted in a finite matter, while continuous is infinite and impossible to count.</p>
<p><strong>Examples:</strong><br>Discrete: # children you want to have, SAT score<br>Continuous: weight, height</p>
</section>
</div>
</figure>
```
